title: 15 Site Walkthrough Questions to Ask Commercial Cleaning Vendors Before They Bid
seoTitle: 15 Site Walkthrough Questions to Ask Commercial Cleaning Vendors
metaDescription: Ask these 15 site walkthrough questions for cleaning vendors to verify 3,500 sq ft/hr production rates, $35–$65/hr labor, and compare bids in our calculator.
excerpt: A 30-minute janitorial site walkthrough determines whether you receive three comparable, transparent bids or three wildly mismatched lump-sum guesses. Ask these 15 operational, pricing, and compliance questions on site to force every estimator to show their labor math and scope inclusions.
quickAnswer: The most effective site walkthrough questions force commercial cleaning vendors to disclose their exact nightly labor hours (benchmarked against ISSA's 3,500 sq ft/hr standard), W-2 versus 1099 workforce status ($35–$65/hr fully burdened labor), 4.33-week monthly billing math, and line-item charges for restrooms ($15–$30/visit), breakrooms ($12–$25/visit), and consumables ($0.012–$0.025/sq ft/visit). Asking all 15 questions during the physical tour locks estimators into apples-to-apples scope assumptions before proposals are submitted.

blocks.text: Most commercial janitorial site walkthroughs fail because the facility manager spends 25 minutes pointing at wastebaskets and restrooms while the sales estimator nods politely, scribbles a rough square-foot number on a notepad, and leaves without committing to a single operational specification. Three days later, the proposals arrive with a 50% price spread and completely incompatible scope definitions. Taking control of the walkthrough with 15 structured site walkthrough questions transforms a passive tour into a rigorous technical audit.
1. Questions 1–4: Labor Hours, ISSA Production Rates & Calendar Math

Ask these four baseline math questions while standing in your main open-plan workspace. They signal immediately that your procurement team understands commercial janitorial cost engineering and will not accept an opaque lump-sum figure.

items: Question 1: 'What exact ISSA production rate (sq ft per labor hour) will you apply to our open office versus our restrooms and breakrooms?' Look for a blended answer between 2,800 and 3,800 sq ft/hr (anchored around the ISSA 3,500 sq ft/hr benchmark). If they cite 5,500+ sq ft/hr, they plan to skip daily vacuuming.

Question 2: 'How many total nightly labor hours and how many technicians will you disclose on the face of your proposal?' Require the estimator to break down cleaner count x shift length (e.g., 2 technicians x 2.25 hours = 4.5 nightly labor hours).

Question 3: 'Does your monthly calculation use the standard 4.33 weeks-per-month factor?' Confirm that 5x/week equals 21.65 visits/month, 3x/week equals 13.0 visits/month, 2x/week equals 8.66 visits/month, and 1x/week equals 4.33 visits/month—with zero 5th-week surcharges.

Question 4: 'Are you bidding on our measured Usable Cleanable Square Footage (USF) or our lease's Rentable Square Footage (RSF)?' Clarify the exact cleanable USF on the spot so no vendor inflates your bid by the landlord's 15% common-area load factor.

blocks.text: 2. Questions 5–8: Flooring Multipliers, Restrooms, Breakrooms & Glass Scope
As you walk from carpeted workstation zones into ceramic-tile restrooms, LVT breakrooms, and glass-walled conference rooms, use Questions 5 through 8 to pin down high-friction scope items.

items: Question 5: 'How do you adjust your labor budget for our specific flooring mix—carpet (1.0x), VCT/LVT vinyl (1.04x), engineered hardwood (1.08x), ceramic tile and grout (1.12x), or polished concrete (0.95x)?' Verify whether they use CRI-certified HEPA backpack vacuums and separate color-coded microfiber mop pads for restrooms versus breakrooms.

Question 6: 'What specific EPA-registered disinfectant and wet dwell time do your crews use in our restrooms, and is restroom care priced inside the base rate ($15–$30/restroom/visit benchmark)?' Most hospital-grade quaternary or hydrogen peroxide disinfectants require a 3-to-10-minute wet contact dwell time to kill pathogens—instant spray-and-wipe fails compliance.

Question 7: 'Does your base quote include daily breakroom sink, countertop, microwave interior, and refrigerator handle sanitization ($12–$25/visit benchmark), plus conference partition glass ($15–$35/visit)?' Make them confirm in writing so these do not turn into post-award change orders.

Question 8: 'How do you price quarterly deep floor care—carpet hot-water extraction and VCT scrub-and-recoat—and can you itemize it separately at $0.03 to $0.06/sq ft/month?' Keeping periodic floor work on a separate line item prevents confusion between turnkey and base-labor bids.

blocks.title: Audit Your Waste Receptacles During the Walkthrough
blocks.text: While walking the lobby, copy rooms, and janitor closet, ask the estimator how your current waste bins affect nightly trash-pull time. Outfitting your Class A lobby and elevator banks with a Safco Public Square 37-Gallon Commercial Steel Receptacle (fire-safe powder-coated steel with an internal liner retainer and architectural square profile) keeps high-visibility zones neat. In tight copy rooms and breakrooms, placing a Rubbermaid Commercial Slim Jim 23-Gallon Recycling & Waste Station (11-inch narrow footprint with integrated venting channels and bag cinches) alongside a janitor-closet Rubbermaid Commercial Brute 44-Gallon Vented Trash Can (NSF-listed LLDPE resin with venting channels that cut liner pull force by 50%) eliminates torn liners and trims 15 to 20 minutes off nightly waste collection.
3. Questions 9–12: W-2 Workforce, COI Liability, Security & OSHA Readiness

Once you reach the janitor closet or facility manager's office, pivot to statutory employment compliance, security screening, and chemical safety. In the $35 to $65/hour standard W-2 labor market, these questions expose low-ball brokers immediately.

items: Question 9: 'Is every cleaner who enters our building a direct W-2 employee on your company payroll, or do you subcontract to 1099 crews or franchise sub-tier operators?' Require an explicit contract warranty prohibiting subcontracting without prior written consent.

Question 10: 'Can you provide a Certificate of Insurance (COI) with $1M/$2M General Liability, statutory Class Code 9014 Workers' Compensation, and a $50,000 Third-Party Janitorial Dishonesty Bond before contract signature?'

Question 11: 'What criminal background check, E-Verify validation, and keycard/alarm check-in protocol do you enforce for night crews?' Ask how they prevent unauthorized guests or prop-open door breaches after hours.
Question 12: 'How will you organize our janitor closet to meet OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1200 Hazard Communication (SDS binder + secondary bottle labels) and Bloodborne Pathogens standards?'

blocks.text: 4. Questions 13–15: Supervision, Backup Staffing & Consumable Supply Logistics
Close the walkthrough with three operational continuity questions that predict what your experience will look like in Month 4—long after the salesperson disappears.

items: Question 13: 'Who is our assigned roving field supervisor, how often do they conduct formal audited inspections on site, and what is your SLA for resolving a missed task?' Look for weekly or biweekly digital QA inspections and a same-day morning recovery guarantee.

Question 14: 'When our regular evening technician calls out sick at 4:00 PM, where does the trained backup floater come from so our building is not skipped?' Reputable BSCs maintain paid mobile floater teams within a 15-mile radius.
Question 15: 'Will you restock our tenant-purchased paper towels, bath tissue, soap, and can liners at zero markup, or itemize turnkey consumables separately ($0.012–$0.025/sq ft/visit)?'

blocks.text: 5. How to Structure Your 30-Minute Vendor Walkthrough Schedule

items.name: Schedule Separate 30-Minute Slots for Three Vetted Bidders
items.text: Avoid cattle-call group walkthroughs where estimators hide their questions. Walk each vendor individually using the exact same printed 15-question sheet and USF floor plan.

items.name: Inspect the Janitor Closet, Restrooms, and Breakroom Together
items.text: Spend 60% of the tour inside high-friction wet zones (restrooms, breakrooms, janitor sink closet) rather than strolling empty carpeted hallways.

items.name: Hand Every Estimator an Identical Bid Response Template
items.text: Require proposals back within 5 business days broken down into base monthly labor (at 4.33 weeks/month), nightly hours, add-on line items, and COI attachment.

faqs.q: Should we share our current janitorial budget or incumbent vendor's price during the walkthrough?
faqs.a: Never disclose your current monthly price during the site walkthrough. If you share your incumbent's rate, estimators will anchor their bid 5% below that number instead of calculating true bottom-up labor hours from your cleanable square footage and fixture counts. Share only your verified USF, service frequency, and exact scope matrix.

faqs.q: Why is it important to ask about secondary chemical bottle labeling during a walkthrough?
faqs.a: Under OSHA Hazard Communication Standard 29 CFR 1910.1200, every spray bottle filled from a bulk chemical dilution station in your janitor closet must display a GHS-compliant secondary label showing product identity and hazard warnings, backed by an accessible Safety Data Sheet (SDS) binder. Unlabeled bottles stored on your premises expose both the vendor and facility to regulatory citations.

faqs.q: What if a vendor refuses to disclose nightly labor hours and insists on outcome-based pricing?
faqs.a: Even outcome-based or fixed-fee contracts rely on an internal labor-hour budget. Disclosing guaranteed minimum nightly labor hours protects you from 'hour shaving,' where a contractor bids 4.5 hours per night during Month 1 and quietly cuts the cleaner's shift to 2.5 hours per night in Month 3 to boost profit margins.

faqs.q: How do frequency multipliers affect the per-visit rate we discuss on the walkthrough?
faqs.a: Soil accumulation decreases per visit as cleaning frequency increases. Relative to a 2x/week baseline (1.00x multiplier, 8.66 visits/mo), 1x/week service carries a 1.08x multiplier (4.33 visits/mo), biweekly carries 1.16x (2.17 visits/mo), and monthly carries 1.28x. Conversely, 3x/week drops to a 0.95x multiplier (13.0 visits/mo) and 5x/week drops to 0.90x (21.65 visits/mo).
